headline: Wyoming Wind Farm Cuts Eagle Deaths by 82% With Smart Camera System
meta_description: A camera system at a Wyoming wind farm automatically slows turbines when eagles approach, reducing fatalities by 82% across 110 turbines.
summary_short: Smart camera technology at a Wyoming wind farm is protecting eagles by automatically slowing turbines when birds approach, cutting deaths dramatically.
body:
A camera system installed at a Wyoming wind farm is automatically slowing turbines when eagles approach, protecting the birds from fatal collisions. A study found the system reduced eagle fatalities by 82% across the farm's 110 turbines—a significant breakthrough in making renewable energy safer for wildlife.

The technology works by detecting approaching birds and triggering turbine slowdowns before impact occurs. This approach addresses a long-standing tension between clean energy production and eagle conservation, as wind farms have historically posed risks to raptors and other flying species.

The success at this Wyoming installation suggests the system could be deployed more widely at wind farms across the country, offering a practical path forward that protects eagles without sacrificing renewable energy generation. The research validates what many conservationists have hoped: that thoughtful engineering can help wind power coexist with vulnerable bird populations.
quick_facts: 82% reduction in eagle fatalities at the Wyoming site
110 turbines equipped with the camera system
Cameras automatically slow turbines when eagles approach
Wyoming wind farm demonstrates wildlife-friendly renewable energy
